name: BP+ Data Capture
description: Records a blood-pressure measurement from a Uscom BP+ device directly into a REDCap instrument, and keeps the device's own result XML as a file on the record. An example module, meant to be copied and edited.
$comment-ajax: An ajax action must be declared for the context it is called from, and a
survey respondent is not logged in -- so save-xml is in both lists.
Undeclared, the framework refuses the call and the recording is silently

project-settings.name:
Instrument that carries the BP+ controls
The unique instrument name, not its label. Blank uses bpplus_measurement.

Field-name prefix
The module writes <prefix>sys, <prefix>dia and the rest. Blank uses bpplus_. Change it only if the fields on your instrument are named differently.

Store the raw measurement XML as a file on the record
Needs a File Upload field named <prefix>xml. A full result runs past 100 kB, which no text field will hold, so this is where the XML belongs.

What to send the device as the patient ID
The device writes this verbatim into its own result file, and keeps it on the SD card when one is fitted — so it is what reconciles a card full of recordings back to records. Send a pseudonym and nothing else: a card is removable and nothing on it is access-controlled.

choices.name: The record ID on its own
Nothing -- the device stores no patient ID

project-settings.name:
Patient ID template
Used when the setting above says so. [record] and [instance] are replaced; everything else is sent as typed. A study code in front keeps one device's card unambiguous when it is shared between projects — but use a neutral code, not one that names the condition being studied.

Largest recording this project will accept (MB)
Blank uses 1, which is many times the size of any real measurement. Anything larger is refused, so the endpoint cannot be used to store arbitrary files. Values outside 0.1 to 16 are brought back inside it.

Set the device clock from this computer when it is out by more than this many minutes
Blank uses 5. The measurement timestamp comes from the device, so a wrong clock mislabels data permanently.

Require the device to be in a particular measurement mode
Refuses to measure when the BP+ reports something else. Leave as Any mode unless the protocol depends on it.

Refuse a measurement started on the device itself
A measurement begun with the BP+'s own Start button carries no patient ID and belongs to no record. On, the module cancels it and says so.

Log every serial line to the browser console
Troubleshooting only.
